scope: Realm Gate masonry, visible ground/threshold contact and architecture/route readability in two previous and two current full static originals only.

inspection.method: All four complete originals opened through view_image; no crops or retouching.

findings.reason: Detail shows broad brown threshold/step pieces suspended above the grass approach, with open space beneath them. Lower gate masonry does not provide a coherent ground union on the right.

Pale masonry, pointed arch, teal/gold banners and cyan lamps identify a gate from approach and detail. The dirt route and full trainer remain readable, though the near bird occupies part of the approach and distant actors gather at the gate.
Broad uniform turf, coarse blade grass and large cliff shelves with sharp triangular dark bands remain below the reference-backed terrain/material finish.

The brown threshold pieces now appear at the grass/path surface rather than as the prominent elevated staircase in the previous detail. The right gate base has a continuous visible masonry extension to the approach surface. These are clearer local ground-contact cues.
findings.local_verdict: PASS for the pictured threshold strips and right base

findings.reason: The left lamp pedestal still ends above the ground, with a dark tree-like vertical form behind/below it rather than a clear masonry-to-ground union. A rock shelf also crosses the lower arch opening. The whole gate/threshold composition therefore still does not read as a clean, coherently grounded architectural entrance.
findings.local_verdict: FAIL for complete entrance contact appearance
findings.limits: This reports the visible junction only, not absence of mechanical support or walkability.

findings.reason: Gate identity and dirt approach remain legible. Trainer body/feet are visible without gross burial. Actors at the entrance obscure part of its lowest central contact, so that concealed segment is unassessed.
Uniform turf, coarse grass blades and broad stepped cliff planes/sharp dark triangular bands retain the full-appearance shortcomings. No large HUD overlay obscures these supplied images.

pair_results.reason: Gate identity/route remain readable in both. Current no longer presents the conspicuous elevated brown staircase at the gate, but the left pedestal/rock-opening union remains visually unresolved. Actor poses and foliage vary; no causal claim.

Ground-level brown strips and the right masonry extension read more continuously than the previous elevated threshold. Left pedestal and rock ledge in the opening still prevent a complete clean-grounded-entrance appearance.

visible_regressions.verdict: No clear new broad architectural/material regression established in these two views
visible_regressions.reason: The principal pictured changes favor threshold/right-base contact. Different actor/foliage poses are not used as evidence of a source change. Hidden central contact is limited by pictured actors.
visible_regressions.limits: Only supplied headings; no all-side absence-of-regression certification.

owning_requirements: Coherent reference-backed masonry/terrain family and readable architecture.
Ground and threshold junctions must look intentionally integrated, without prominent suspended entrance pieces.
Readable trainer and route; these stills do not certify mechanics or complete traversal.
limits: Static pictured appearance only. No mechanical support, collision, walkability, earned route, movement, timing or implementation cause inferred.
Only approach and detail-crag, day as supplied. No other headings, weather, night/Medium, fight, device, performance, whole row, full matrix or whole criterion claim.
Lower central junction is partly obscured by actors; concealed/rear/underside junctions remain unassessed.
No prior numeric grades or catalogue rerating. Original 253bd overall FAIL, five Bridge full-bar FAIL results and all other witnesses remain untouched.
Current preference is bounded local contact readability, not a full-bar PASS or READY.
